title.narrative: Social Protection mechanisms especially amongst vulnerable groups enhanced

description.narrative: In Kenya, large segments of the population; particularly informal economy workers, persons with disabilities, refugees, migrant workers, and people living with HIV, remain insufficiently covered by social protection systems. Under the Decent Work Country Programme, the ILO supports national efforts to develop inclusive, adequate, and sustainable social protection, aligned with Article 43 of the Constitution of Kenya, which guarantees socio-economic rights for all. The strategy focuses on expanding coverage, improving benefit adequacy, and strengthening policy, legal, and institutional frameworks to ensure access to essential services. Key priorities include universal health coverage, inclusive pension and unemployment insurance systems, and integration of marginalized groups, especially rural and informal economy workers, into national protection schemes. Expected results include increased policy coherence, institutional capacity, and coordination across relevant stakeholders. Pilot initiatives support extending protection to informal workers, establishing a universal disability benefit, and enhancing access for refugees. The programme also promotes sustainable financing, digital solutions, and improved governance of social protection. Implemented in collaboration with national institutions, UN partners, and development actors, the initiative seeks to achieve a more inclusive, equitable, and resilient social protection system by 2025.
